title: normalize runs branch-free and in parallel
body:
`normalize` in `libsufr/src/build.rs` is the first pass over the text. For each byte it tests `is_ascii_lowercase`, then tests `ignore_softmask` to pick `N` or the upper-case byte, and sets `occupancy[byte]`. It runs on one thread. `find_n_ranges`, run right after it for DNA with `allow_ambiguity`, is a second single-threaded pass over the same bytes.

On `benchmarks/runs/dna-1024.fa` (1 GiB, 4 threads, page cache warm) the log stamps the read at 21:13:59 and the bucket count at 21:14:00, so `normalize`, `keep_table` and `find_n_ranges` together take at most about a second of a 12.7 s build. The log has no line of its own for `normalize`.

## Proposal

- Build a 256-entry table once from the alphabet. Lower-case bytes map to `N` or to their upper-case byte, every other byte to itself. The loop becomes `*b = table[*b as usize]` and `occupancy[*b as usize] = true`, with no branch per byte.
- Split the text with `par_chunks_mut`, one `occupancy` per chunk, reduced with OR.

## Open

Whether `find_n_ranges` rides the same pass. A run of `N` can cross a chunk boundary, so the parallel version needs a join step. CLAUDE.md names `normalize` as the pass that other per-byte work rides on.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/fdde2c6d
notes.text: Done in the working tree, not yet committed: a 256-entry table from the alphabet, applied over par_chunks_mut(CHUNK_SIZE) with one occupancy per chunk ORed in the reduce, and a log line for the pass. On benchmarks/runs/dna-1024.fa at 4 threads, three runs each: 208, 208 and 212 ms before, 75, 78 and 76 ms after. The .sufr outputs are identical. find_n_ranges is still its own pass; whether it rides this one is the open question.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/fdde2c6d
notes.text: find_n_ranges stays its own pass and is now parallel, in the working tree and not committed. Each chunk keeps its runs of 1000 or more plus any run touching a chunk end, the reduce joins a run across a boundary, and a final retain drops the short ones. On long-n-1024.fa with --dna -a at 4 threads, three runs: 252, 321 and 265 ms before, 59, 60 and 59 ms after. The log reports 3 runs, which an independent count confirms, and the outputs are identical. A first attempt folded the scan into normalize; Jack wanted the passes kept separate, and the fold cost 33 ms per GiB on the path with no N tracking.
